COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
09.03.2026 SPA No.37 of 2026
Vinod Kumar & Others … Appellants
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand & Others … Respondents 
Hon’ble Manoj Kumar Gupta, C. J.
Hon’ble Subhash Upadhyay, J.
1. Mr. Deepak Kumar, appellant no.2, party￾in-person.
2. Mr. B.S. Parihar, learned Additional C.S.C. 
for the State.
3. Mr. Pankaj Miglani, learned counsel for 
respondent no.3.
4. At the outset, Shri Pankaj Miglani, learned 
counsel appearing on behalf of respondent no.3 
has raised a preliminary objection to the 
maintainability of the instant appeal on behalf of 
appellant nos.1 and 3, on the ground, that 
appellant no.2, who appears in person, cannot 
represent appellant nos.1 and 3.
5. On such objection being raised, appellant 
no.2 in person states that he may be permitted to 
delete appellant nos.1 and 3 from the memo of 
appeal. 
6. Accordingly, he is permitted to delete 
appellant nos.1 and 3 from the memo of appeal 
and to array appellant no.2 as appellant no.1. Delay Condonation Application IA No.2/2026
7. The appeal is reported to be beyond time by 
3 days. The cause shown for the delay is found to 
be satisfactory and, accordingly, delay is 
condoned. Delay Condonation Application stands 
disposed of. Office is directed to allot a regular 
number to the instant appeal. 
SPA No.37 of 2026
8. Learned State Counsel as well as learned 
counsel for respondent no.3 is granted four 
weeks’ time to file counter affidavit. 
9. List thereafter.
10. Office is also directed to correct computer 
database in view of the instant order. 
(Subhash Upadhyay, J.) (Manoj Kumar Gupta, C.J.) 
 09.03.2026 09.03.2026 
Rajni
